title: The lockmark
instruction: Draw the lockmark from its master, and place it only in its four fixed places.
intro: Democracy has a structure. The lockmark draws it as nine nodes joined by links, with the lever, a larger red node at bottom right, at the place where one change moves the rest. It signs our work in four fixed places: the masthead, the page header, the footer and the sign-off.
Its drawing never changes, and it codes nothing. Chapter 11 sets how a tracker shows a bill’s steps, and a series or a pillar is named in words.

rules.title: Draw the lockmark from its master for its size, and keep its drawing fixed.
rules.rule: The lockmark is a 3 by 3 grid of nodes joined around its edge and through its center, with the lever in signature red at bottom right. Place the 16 px master from 16 to 23 px, the 24 px master from 24 to 47 px and the display master, drawn for our brand guide’s fifth edition, from 48 px.

why.text: At small sizes our fifth edition’s single master lost its shape: at 24 px only 5 percent of its ink was solid, and at 16 px the lever became one pink pixel. The small masters set every node and link on whole pixels and draw the lever one size up, so it still reads as the place where one change moves the rest.

correct.caption: The lockmark’s construction at 240 px, then at true size at 96, 48, 24 and 16 px, and at 48 px on Charcoal and on Prussian.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s master scaled to 16 px beside the 16 px master. Its nodes shrink to the width of a link and the lever turns into a single pink pixel.

specs.label: Lever
specs.value: Radius 4.75 units, bottom right, signature red

specs.label: Links
specs.value: 1 px Stone around the edge and through the center

specs.label: 16 px master
specs.value: Centers at 2.5, 7.5 and 12.5 px; 3 px nodes; 5 px lever

specs.label: 24 px master
specs.value: Centers at 3.5, 11.5 and 19.5 px; 5 px nodes; 7 px lever

rules.builders: The lockmark files read --link for the links and --lever for the lever. Leave the lever on the signature token; on Prussian, place the White file. Ask the editor for the display master, which keeps our fifth edition’s drawing.

rules.title: Place the lockmark only in its four places, once in a view.
rules.rule: The lockmark signs four places, at the size each one sets: the masthead, where L3 sets it beside the wordmark (Rule 03.6); the page header of a report or slide page, 24 px beside the section label; the footer, 24 px beside the tagline or 16 px beside a chart’s source line; and the sign-off, 48 px from the display master at the bottom right of a social card, cover or poster. A view shows it once, so when a masthead and a footer share a view, the footer keeps it.

why.text: A signature works by turning up in the same place at the same size, so a reader finds it without looking. Each size keeps the drawing crisp: the 24 and 16 px masters sit on whole pixels, and the sign-off takes the display master because the 24 px master turns soft when enlarged to 40 px. Used as a bullet or scattered as decoration, the lockmark stops signing the page.
why.basis: Dustin Cathcart’s ruling on the lockmark, November 7, 2026; Design judgment

correct.caption: The four places at true size: a 768 px site masthead with L3; a report page header with the lockmark at 24 px beside the section label; a footer with the lockmark at 24 px beside the tagline, and a chart’s footer with it at 16 px beside the source line; and the bottom-right corner of a 1080 px social card with the lockmark at 48 px inside the 72 px margin.

failure.caption: The lockmark used as list bullets on a flyer, three lockmarks in one view, each one decoration.

specs.label: Masthead
specs.value: L3 on screens from 48em, 768 px at the default text size, and in the email header: the 24 px wordmark master with the lockmark at 52 px from its display master (Rule 03.6)

specs.label: Page header
specs.value: 24 px beside the section label on report and slide pages; 0.25 in in print

specs.label: Footer
specs.value: 24 px beside the tagline at the foot of a page or an email; 16 px beside the source line in a chart’s footer. L6, the strip that closes a report, carries it at L6’s own proportion (Rule 03.2)

specs.label: Sign-off
specs.value: 48 px from the display master, bottom right of social cards, covers and posters, inside the margin; 0.50 in in print

specs.label: Once in a view
specs.value: When a masthead and a footer share one view, the footer keeps the lockmark and the masthead sets the wordmark alone

specs.label: Favicon
specs.value: Never the lockmark: favicons use ampersand B’s 16 px master (Rule 03.4)

rules.builders: Pick the master by the size the place sets: the 24 px master in page headers and footers, the 16 px master in a chart’s footer, and the display master for the sign-off and inside L3. Ask the editor for the display master’s file.

rules.title: Let the lockmark code nothing.
rules.rule: Draw the lockmark the same in every place, with no node lit, dimmed, moved or added. It never shows how far a bill has moved, which series a piece belongs to or which pillar a piece serves. Each of those jobs has its own sign: a bill’s steps are numbered, as chapter 11 sets them; a series is named in words in the kicker (Rule 01.21); and a pillar takes its icon with its word beside it.

why.text: One drawing with one job is easy to learn. Our fifth edition used the same nine nodes to code a bill’s stage, a series, a pillar and a kind of content, and a reader could not tell which code a grid carried, or whether the mark in the masthead meant anything at all. Numbers and words do those jobs better, because a reader can say “step 4 of 6” out loud and words survive gray print.
why.basis: Dustin Cathcart’s ruling on the lockmark, November 7, 2026; Design judgment

correct.caption: A bill in a tracker list as Rule 11.5 draws it, at true size on a 358 px phone column: six numbered steps, the fourth marked as the step the bill is at, with the step in words beside them. No lockmark sits in the row.

failure.caption: The same bill drawn on the lockmark’s nine nodes, four of them filled to show progress. Nine nodes cannot count six steps, a reader has to decode the filled ones, and the mark that signs our pages changes from bill to bill.

specs.label: Drawing
specs.value: The same in every place: nine nodes, their links and the red lever

specs.label: A bill’s progress
specs.value: Numbered steps with the step in words; Rule 11.5

specs.label: A series
specs.value: Its name in words in the kicker; Rule 01.21

specs.label: A pillar
specs.value: Its icon with its word beside it; chapter 09

specs.label: Patterns
specs.value: None: the lockmark appears whole or not at all

rules.builders: Take the grid out of any template that used it for a tracker, a series, a pillar or a state, and take each job from the chapter that now holds it. Chapter 11 sets the tracker’s steps, their sizes and their words, and Rule 11.5 sets them in lists.

sources: “Democracy has a structure.” is the lockmark’s explanatory line, approved by Dustin Cathcart in October 2026.
